title: Robotics club wins provincial championship
author: R. Sharma
excerpt: Our senior robotics team took first place at the Lumbini Province School Robotics Challenge.
body: We are proud to share that our senior robotics club won first place at the Lumbini Province School Robotics Challenge in Butwal.
The team of six students designed, built and programmed a line-following rescue robot over three months in the STEAM Lab, competing against fourteen schools from across the province.
Congratulations to the team and to their mentors. The winning robot will be on display at the Science & Innovation Fair in September.

title: New reading wing opens in the library
author: S. Gurung
excerpt: Three hundred new books and a dedicated quiet reading corner for primary students.
body: Our library has grown. A new reading wing adds three hundred titles in Nepali and English and a dedicated quiet corner designed for primary students.
The wing was made possible by our parent community's book drive. Thank you — every shelf tells your generosity.

title: Meet our new science faculty
author: R. Sharma
excerpt: Three new teachers join the science department this academic year.
body: Three new teachers join our science department this year, bringing experience in physics, biology and laboratory practice.
Full profiles and a short interview with each of them will be published here before classes begin.

title: STEAM week recap
author: P. Thapa
excerpt: Five days, every grade, one question: how does it actually work?
body: STEAM week closed with an exhibition in the school hall after five days of cross-grade projects — bridges built from bamboo, a hand-cranked water pump, stop-motion films and a scale model of the Deukhuri valley.
Every class presented its work to another grade, which is the part students tell us they remember most: explaining an idea until someone younger understands it.

title: Monsoon safety reminders
author: S. Gurung
excerpt: Transport timings and pickup arrangements during heavy rainfall.
body: During heavy rainfall, school transport runs on adjusted timings and some valley routes may be shortened to the nearest safe stop.
Families are informed by phone on any day routes change. Students are never sent home early without a confirmed guardian.
